rule: Review КТ5: every provision whose draft open point is implementation_only is read against the pinned text before it is counted as resolvable or covered. 'confirmed': the text fixes what is required and no author choice is needed; the lab adds a check. 'reclassified': an author decision or a missing definition blocks it; origin_after names it. A checkable correction is recorded with the decision.
closure_rule: Review of checkpoint 6: for each confirmed provision the draft open point (implementation_only) is closed once the missing lab check exists, unless something else remains. 'closed': the agent's reading answers the draft need from the text (answer); decision_status becomes NONE_IDENTIFIED by agent reading, the open point is removed, and the draft classification and reason stay in this record. 'open': a missing formula, an undefined criterion, an external artifact or a contested reading remains; the open point stays with that origin and reason. A partial check (coverage PARTIAL) is a limit of coverage, not an open point. Nothing here is a human acceptance (A6).
reading_rule: Review of checkpoint 6: the remaining open points of uncovered provisions, whose origin was a Codex draft, are read one by one against the pinned corpus (all 38 documents), as the implementation_only drafts were. 'kept': the draft origin holds; the open point stays, now as the lab's reading; partial_check says whether a clear core could be checked without deciding the open point. 'reclassified': another origin blocks it (origin_after). 'returned': the corpus settles what the draft said was missing (most often a reference to a corpus document read as external); the provision is resolvable (implementation_only) and needs a lab check; once the check exists it carries a closure like a confirmed decision. Nothing here is a human acceptance (A6).
core_revision_rule: Review КТ7-GPT-01: a provision marked partial_check: true is unfinished work while it is uncovered. Each such clear part is checked, or, when the check cannot confirm it (the part would be checked only as a label, needs the open point itself, or needs a change to the published bench), the flag is set to false with an individual reason; the earlier value and the reason stay in partial_check_revised. No flag is dropped to regain a stage status.

closure.answer: The Code makes it concrete: no office appoints the function, and its rules change only through UPGRADE with simulation (A.1a).

items.quote: Crisis mode does not create new powers. It temporarily constrains execution pathways to preserve survival and reversibility.
items.reason: Concretized as CRISIS-2-02 (closed): a new right, obligation or authority created in crisis is a recorded act; 'temporarily' is the exit of §9.

draft_need: Declare a power-comparison model and survival and reversibility predicates.
closure.coverage_limit: Powers are observed as definitions and authority notices; 'temporarily' as nothing outliving the exit.
closure.answer: Concretized by §2 (no new rights, obligations or authorities) and §9 (the crisis ends at its exit conditions).

items.quote:

items.reason: Precedent, custom, interpretation rule and future authorization are observable as records after the exit that cite a crisis action, state a rule derived from it, or keep an authority; 'outside an explicitly declared Crisis Scope' is the time after exit and any other scope. Custom formed without any record is not observable (partial).

draft_need: Declare how normative reliance and interpretive effects are represented.
closure.coverage_limit: Observed after the exit: citations of crisis actions, recorded interpretation rules, authority notices. Custom formed without a record is not observable.
closure.answer: Normative reliance = citation, recorded rule or authority after exit (§6 Non-Precedent Rule lists the uses).

items.quote: Crisis mode prioritizes survival, containment, and reversibility over optimization, efficiency, or growth.
items.reason: Resolving conflicts between objectives needs an effects model. Core: no crisis action states optimization, efficiency or growth as its objective.

items.quote:
All Crisis execution operates strictly within a Crisis Scope Envelope.

The Crisis Scope Envelope is a hard operational subset of DKP-7-SCOPE-001 and defines the maximal permissible actions, authorities, and interpretations allowed during Crisis execution.
items.reason: The draft calls SCOPE absent, but DKP-7-SCOPE-001 is in the corpus and bounds Crisis Scope (§5: survival-oriented, minimized authority, no permanent state change, five explicit prohibitions). An action outside the declared envelope or the §5 limits is observable.

draft_need: Declare a representation and membership test for scope envelopes.
closure.coverage_limit: The envelope is a declared list of §6 actions; S1 membership per SCOPE §3 (H-CR-5).
closure.answer: SCOPE is in the corpus: §5 bounds Crisis Scope inside S1 and §3 classifies S1; the envelope is declared at entry.

items.quote: The Crisis Scope Envelope SHALL NOT be expanded, inferred, or bypassed under any circumstances.
items.reason: The envelope is declared (§1: a hard subset of SCOPE); expansion is an action outside the declared list, inference is an envelope not declared at entry or changed later, bypass is an action without it. All observable with the envelope as an input.

draft_need: Declare scope comparison rules and authorization provenance semantics.
closure.coverage_limit: The envelope is a declared list of §6 actions (input crisis_envelope).
closure.answer: Expansion, inference and bypass are relative to the declared envelope; the content of the envelope is the subject of §1's other sentences, not of this one.

items.quote:
- only upon escalation from DKP-3-DEFENSE-001 or equivalent L3 containment protocols,
- upstream of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 (when recovery is possible).
items.reason: Not only the undefined ordering with UPGRADE: 'only upon escalation from DKP-3-DEFENSE-001 or equivalent L3 containment protocols' meets §4 triggers that no L3 protocol escalates (an execution-error cascade, a PTL divergence); verified as author question Q-065, the same reading question as CRISIS-0-01. items.quote:

- DKP-4-CRISIS-001 SHALL NOT introduce new rights, obligations, or authorities.
items.reason: Two hard constraints: no axiom redefinition, no new rights, obligations or authorities. A crisis output defining one of them, or an authority granted during the crisis, is observable.

draft_need: Declare how redefinitions and newly introduced normative effects are detected.

closure.answer: Redefinitions and new rights, obligations or authorities are recorded acts of the crisis layer.

items.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus (§4-§5 give the boundaries). A crisis act that creates rights, extends authority duration, modifies axioms, generates precedent or interprets 'minimum required conditions' outside the declared Crisis Scope is observable (cf. CRISIS-2-02, -2-05 closed).

draft_need: Declare how the applicability effects of logic and interpretations are represented.
closure.coverage_limit: SCOPE §3-§5 boundaries observed as S1 membership, the declared region, new rights, outliving authority and precedent.
closure.answer: SCOPE §3-§5 give the boundaries: S1 only, the declared Crisis Scope, no new rights, no authority beyond the crisis, no precedent.

items.quote: No crisis condition, trigger, state, or action SHALL be extrapolated, generalized, or reused outside the explicitly declared Crisis Scope.
items.reason: Reuse outside the explicitly declared Crisis Scope is observable when the scope is declared: an action applied to another region or domain.

draft_need: Declare artifact provenance and scope-membership semantics.
closure.coverage_limit: The Crisis Scope is a declared region; reuse in another region is observed.
closure.answer: Scope membership is relative to the declared Crisis Scope; reuse outside it is a recorded act.

items.quote: A Crisis is a PTL-confirmed system state in which L3 containment and correction mechanisms are insufficient to prevent imminent or ongoing violation of Axiom A1 or Axiom A2.
items.reason: L3 insufficiency and imminence need a model.

items.reason: The condition classes need measured models and a duration.

items.quote: C0 – Normal Operation No crisis conditions present.
items.reason: C0 is defined by the absence of crisis conditions; whether a C0 step coexists with a PTL-confirmed trigger (§4) or a crisis action is recomputable from the PTL observations. Only this direction is fixed: leaving C0 also needs the §9 exit conditions.

draft_need: Declare a complete crisis-condition evaluator for the simulated domain.
closure.answer: Crisis conditions are the §4 PTL-confirmed triggers; C0 is their absence.

items.quote: C1 – Emergency Containment Immediate life-preserving actions activated. Strict prioritization of survival-critical resources.
items.reason: Life-preserving and survival-critical classes need evidence.

items.reason: Essential functions and the core boundary are not defined.

items.reason: The feasible set for maximum containment is not defined.

items.reason: Truth preservation and collapse need a model.

items.reason: Non-essential and non-critical are not defined. Core: crisis actions belong to the §6 list.

items.reason: Each purpose or either purpose is open. Core: every rationing act cites life or core execution.

items.quote:
- conceal actions or decisions from audit,
- use Crisis as justification for permanent control or emergency governance,
- apply utilitarian valuation of human life.
items.reason: Three bans, each observable: a crisis action without an audit commitment, staying in crisis after the exit conditions hold (permanent control), rationing by a utility valuation of life.

draft_need: Declare an authoritative execution trace and classifiers for the prohibited governance and valuation practices.
closure.coverage_limit: Permanence observed as staying in crisis once the module's exit conditions hold; 'emergency governance' as authority notices (also §7, §9).
closure.answer: Audit commitment, the §9 exit conditions and the §7 allocation bases fix the three tests.

items.quote:
Crisis governance is algorithmic only.

No emergency human authority is created.
items.reason: 'Algorithmic only' is concretized by §8 itself: all actions derive from pre-defined protocol logic; no emergency human authority. Both are observable (derivation from the CRISIS state determination; authority notices; human-directed actions).

draft_need: Declare how algorithmic derivation and pre-definition are verified.
closure.answer: §8 itself: every crisis action derives from pre-defined protocol logic; human intervention is a logged perturbation.

items.quote:
- transition to DKP-4-UPGRADE-001,
- controlled system partition or termination.
items.reason: Handoff and terminal-state contracts are not defined.

items.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus (§4: interpretation only within a declared Crisis Scope, bounded by SCOPE), but which mechanism may interpret when crisis execution logic may not stays open. Core: no interpretation of 'minimum required conditions' outside a declared Crisis Scope.
